brief.headline: Offer 15-day faster payment in exchange for a 12% price cut — their 12.16% borrowing cost shows cash is worth that much to them, and faster terms ease their stretched 101d cash cycle

priceAsk.summary: Ask for a price reduction in exchange for accelerated payment, targeting a discount roughly equal to their borrowing cost
priceAsk.basis: Their borrowing cost is 12.16% and their cash conversion cycle runs at 101d versus peer median of 64d — paying faster saves them real interest expense and eases their stretched working capital

paymentTermAsk.summary: Offer to move from 30 Days After Receipt to 15 Days After Receipt in exchange for the price cut
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: ₹26.60 L working capital freed if we move 15 days faster

brief.financialLeverage: Shrinath runs a thin 2.3% net margin against peer median of 2.5%, carries debt at 1.25x debt-to-equity, and sits in the grey zone with Altman Z-score of 2.36 — financial stress is real. Interest coverage of 1.94x is tight. Their 101d cash cycle runs 37 days longer than the 64d peer median, and they already stretch their own suppliers to 51d versus peer 40d. Our ₹6.47 Cr spend is just 0.61% of their ₹1064.86 Cr revenue, so we have no volume hammer. EPF payment delays flag operational stress. Push hard on payment-for-price swap (cash is oxygen for them), but avoid a brutal margin squeeze that tips a fragile supplier into real distress and threatens our supply.

evidence.point: Their effective borrowing cost shows cash has a clear price
Their cash conversion cycle runs well above the industry median
Tight interest coverage leaves little cushion for rate shocks or revenue dips
BOPET film import benchmark provides a substrate cost reference
Altman Z-score places them in the grey zone between safe and distress
EPF payment delays signal working-capital strain

risks: Altman Z of 2.36 puts them in grey zone — pressing too hard on price risks tipping them into distress and losing our laminate supply
Our ₹6.47 Cr is only 0.61% of their ₹1064.86 Cr revenue, so we have almost no volume leverage to force compliance
EPF payment delays and tight 1.94x interest coverage suggest cash is already stretched — a payment-term extension (instead of acceleration) would worsen their position
Thin 2.3% net margin leaves no room for deep price cuts without pushing them into loss — frame the ask as a payment-speed swap, not a margin haircut
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We'd like to help ease your 101-day cash cycle by moving to 15-day payment — and in return, we're looking for a price adjustment that reflects the 12.16% cost of capital you're currently paying.
